Johnson Sr. | hq_location = [[San Mateo, California]], U.S. | website = {{URL|franklinresources.com}} | footnotes = Financials {{as of|2025|09|30|lc=y|df=US}}.{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/38777/000003877725000238/ben-20250930.htm |title=Franklin Templeton: FY 2025 Annual Report |publisher=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission |date=November 10, 2025}} }} '''Franklin Resources, Inc.''' is an American [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[investment management]] [[holding company]] that, together with its subsidiaries, is referred to as '''Franklin Templeton'''; it is a global [[investment firm]] founded in [[New York City]] in 1947 as Franklin Distributors, Inc. It is listed on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] under the [[ticker symbol]] BEN, in honor of [[Benjamin Franklin]], for whom the company is named, and who was admired by founder Rupert Johnson Sr. The firm became the world's largest asset managers, providing services operating in 150 countries. In 1973, the company's headquarters moved from New York to [[San Mateo, California]].{{Cite web |title=Our History |url=https://www.franklinresources.com/about-us/history |access-date=January 3, 2024 |website=Franklinresources.com |language=en}} ==History== The company was founded in 1947 in New York by Rupert H. (Harris) Johnson Sr. (1900–1989), who ran a successful retail brokerage firm from an office on Wall Street.Eric John Abrahamson and Grant Alger, Persistence and Perspective: Franklin Templeton Investments: The First Sixty Years (San Mateo: Franklin Resources, Inc., 2007, xvii He named the company for American polymath [[Benjamin Franklin]] because Franklin espoused frugality and prudence when it came to saving and investing.{{cite news |last=Knapp |first=Gwen |title=Charles Johnson, top Giants owner, keeps low profile |newspaper=San Francisco Gate |date=September 29, 2012 |url=http://www.sfgate.com/giants/article/Charles-Johnson-top-Giants-owner-keeps-low-3466803.php |access-date=April 28, 2016}} The company's first line of mutual funds, Franklin Custodian Funds, was a series of conservatively managed equity and bond funds designed to appeal to most investors. After Rupert Sr. retired, his son, [[Charles B. Johnson]] (Charlie), took over as president and chief executive officer in 1957 at age 24. At that time, the funds had total assets under management of US$2.5 million.{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/SF-Giants-owner-gave-1K-to-PAC-behind-racist-ad-13321897.php|title=SF Giants owner gave $1K to PAC behind racist ad targeting black voters|date=October 19, 2018|last=Ravani|first=Sarah|website=San Francisco Chronicle|access-date=February 14, 2019}} [[Rupert Johnson Jr.]], Charlie's brother, joined the company in 1965.[https://www.forbes.com/profile/rupert-johnson-jr/ Forbes: The World's Billionaires: "Rupert Johnson Jr."] April 2015 Franklin went public in 1971.{{cite news |url=https://dealbook.nytimes.com/2013/09/30/mutual-fund-billionaire-gives-250-million-to-yale/|title=Mutual Fund Billionaire Gives $250 Million to Yale|date=September 30, 2013|last=Alden|first=William|newspaper=[[New York Times]] |access-date=February 10, 2019}} In 1973, the company acquired Winfield & Company, a [[San Mateo, California|San Mateo]], California-based investment firm, and moved Franklin's offices from [[New York City|New York]] to California. The combined organization had close to US$250 million in assets under management and approximately 60 employees. In 1979, Franklin Money Fund began a growth surge that made it Franklin's first billion-dollar fund and launched the company's significant asset growth in the 1980s. Starting in 1980, the company's total assets under management doubled (or nearly doubled) every year for the next six years. The company's stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in 1986. In the same year, the company opened its first office outside North America in Taiwan. In 1988, Franklin acquired L.F. Rothschild Fund Management Company. Assets under management for Franklin grew from just over US$2 billion in 1982 to more than US$40 billion in 1989 (the crash of 1987 had little impact on Franklin's income and bond funds).{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}} In October 1992, Franklin acquired Templeton, Galbraith & Hansberger Ltd. for a reported cost of $913 million, leading to the common name '''Franklin Templeton'''.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/business/1992/08/01/franklin-templeton-to-form-mutual-giant/aa89d736-7a8d-494d-805e-22134db12e87/ |title=Franklin, Templeton to form mutual fund giant |date=August 1, 1992 |last=Fatsis |first= Stefan |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |access-date=September 20, 2021}} [[Mutual fund]] pioneer [[John Templeton|Sir John Templeton]] was the owner of Templeton, Galbraith & Hansberger Ltd together with his son Dr. John Templeton and John Galbraith who together owned 70% of the firm.[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ywUQAAAAIBAJ&sjid=d5ADAAAAIBAJ&dq=templeton%20galbraith%20%26%20hansberger&pg=3366%2C177263 "Franklin to acquire Templeton mutual fund"]''[[Business Times (Kuala Lumpur)|Business Times]]'' (August 3, 1992) {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314131124/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ywUQAAAAIBAJ&sjid=d5ADAAAAIBAJ&dq=templeton%20galbraith%20%26%20hansberger&pg=3366%2C177263 |date=March 14, 2016}} In November 1996, Heine Securities Corporation, known for the Mutual Series of funds, merged into the Franklin Templeton complex. In October 2000, Franklin acquired Bissett Funds to increase its Canadian presence, and Bissett remains a key brand from Franklin in the Canadian market. The Fiduciary Trust Company was acquired by Franklin Templeton in April 2001.Eric John Abrahamson and Grant Alger, Persistence and Perspective: Franklin Templeton Investments: The First Sixty Years (San Mateo: Franklin Resources, Inc., 2007) [[Fiduciary Trust Company International]], a member of the Franklin family, maintained an office of over 650 employees in [[2 World Trade Center (1971–2001)|2 World Trade Center]] at the time of the [[September 11 attacks]] in 2001.[https://www.franklintempleton.com/retail/jsp_cm/corp/press/2001/world_trade_091301.jsp Franklin Templeton] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711022949/https://www.franklintempleton.com/retail/jsp_cm/corp/press/2001/world_trade_091301.jsp |date=July 11, 2011}} Update on employees and operations. September 13, 2001 87 employees died in the collapse.[https://www.franklintempleton.com/retail/jsp_cm/corp/press/2001/friq4_102501.jsp Franklin Templeton] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041125200759/https://www.franklintempleton.com/retail/jsp_cm/corp/press/2001/friq4_102501.jsp |date=November 25, 2004}} Quarterly earnings press release. October 25, 2001.{{cite web | url=http://interactive.wsj.com/public/resources/documents/Tenant-List.htm | title=A Look at Former World Trade Center Tenants | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=January 18, 2002 | access-date=August 20, 2012 | archive-date=July 31, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140731081614/http://interactive.wsj.com/public/resources/documents/Tenant-List.htm | url-status=dead }} The firm has specialized expertise across a full range of asset classes. It offers products under the Franklin, Templeton, Mutual Series and Fiduciary brand names, among others. Like other large investment companies, the firm offers a wide variety of funds but is traditionally best known for bond funds under the Franklin brand, international funds under the Templeton brand, and value funds under the Mutual Series brand. In April 2007, Franklin Resources was 445th in the [[Fortune 500]], and 7th overall among securities companies.[https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune500/2007/snapshots/541.html CNN Money]{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Fortune 500 snapshot, April 2007. The same month, ''[[USA Today]]'' listed BEN stock as the top stock pick for the last 25 years based on returns, claiming it is up 64,224% since 1982.[https://www.usatoday.com/money/top25-stocks.htm USA Today] ''If Only I Had Bought'', April 16, 2007. As of July 31, 2008, Franklin Resources, Inc. managed over $570 billion in total assets worldwide.[http://www.franklintempleton.com/share/pdf/pressrelease/FRI_AUM_PR0708.pdf Franklin Templeton] Press release. August 11, 2008. In February 2009, ''[[Barron's Magazine]]'' called Franklin Templeton "King of the Decade" among fund families over the ten-year period ending in 2008.Barron's. ''The Best Families in a Bruising Year'' by Tom Sullivan. February 2, 2009. In 2013, Charles Johnson retired as chairman and his son [[Greg Johnson (businessman)|Greg Johnson]] became chairman of the board, CEO and president.{{cite web|url=https://dealbook.nytimes.com/2013/09/30/mutual-fund-billionaire-gives-250-million-to-yale/|title=Mutual Fund Billionaire Gives $250 Million to Yale |date=September 30, 2013|last=Alden|first=William|website=DealBook|access-date=February 10, 2019}} In 2019, the firm acquired Benefit Street Partners, an alternative credit investment group.{{cite web|url=https://investors.franklinresources.com/news-center/press-releases/press-release-details/2018/Franklin-Templeton-Investments-Announces-Acquisition-of-Alternative-Credit-Manager-Benefit-Street-Partners/default.aspx |title=Franklin Templeton Investments Announces Acquisition of Alternative Credit Manager Benefit Street Partners|date=October 25, 2018}} In 2020, [[Jenny Johnson (businesswoman)|Jenny Johnson]] became CEO and President of the firm and Greg Johnson became Executive chairman. Franklin Templeton acquired AdvisorEngine in May 2020, completing the deal in September 2022. Founded 2014 by Rich Cancro, the wealth management technology platform provides advisors with CRM, portfolio management, client portal, and digital onboarding tools, enhancing Franklin Templeton's digital wealth management offerings.{{Cite web|url=https://www.institutionalinvestor.com/article/2aucw8wgcjxkym0kdlse8/ria-intel/why-franklin-templeton-acquired-advisorengine|title=Why Franklin Templeton Acquired AdvisorEngine | Institutional Investor|website=Institutionalinvestor.com|access-date=August 1, 2026}} In July 2020, Franklin Templeton acquired [[Legg Mason|Legg Mason, Inc.]], making Franklin Templeton one of the world's largest independent, specialized global investment managers, with a combined $1.4 trillion in assets under management (AUM). The combined footprint deepened Templeton's presence in key geographies and created an expansive investment platform that includes institutional and retail client AUM.{{Cite web|url=https://investors.franklinresources.com/news-center/press-releases/press-release-details/2020/Franklin-Templeton-Completes-Acquisition-of-Legg-Mason/default.aspx|title= Franklin Templeton Completes Acquisition of Legg Mason|website=Franklin Resources|date=July 31, 2020}} In November 2021, Franklin Templeton announced its acquisition of [[Lexington Partners]] in a $1.75{{nbsp}}billion cash deal.{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/franklin-templeton-buy-lexington-partners-175-bln-part-secondaries-push-2021-11-01/ |title=Franklin Templeton to buy Lexington Partners for $1.75 bln as part of secondaries push |date=November 1, 2021 |work=[[Reuters]] |first1=Niket |last1=Nishant |first2=Chibuike |last2=Oguh}} The acquisition completed in April 2022.{{cite web | url=https://www.privatebankerinternational.com/news/franklin-templeton-lexington-partners-deal/ | title=Franklin Templeton finalises takeover of Lexington Partners | date=April 5, 2022 }} In January 2022, Franklin Templeton acquired O'Shaughnessy Asset Management, an asset management firm founded by [[James O'Shaughnessy (investor)|James O'Shaughnessy]].{{cite press release|title=Franklin Templeton Completes Acquisition of O'Shaughnessy Asset Management, a Leading Custom Indexing Provider Through Its Canvas(R) Platform|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/franklin-templeton-completes-acquisition-o-140000063.html|publisher=[[Business Wire]]|via=[[Yahoo! Finance]]|date=January 4, 2022}} On May 31, 2022, it was announced that [[BNY Mellon Investment Management]] would sell Alcentra to Franklin Templeton. The transaction was completed on November 1, 2022.{{Cite web |date=May 31, 2022 |title=Franklin Templeton buys BNY Mellon subsidiary Alcentra |url=https://www.internationalinvestment.net/news/4050630/franklin-templeton-buys-bny-mellon-subsidiary-alcentra |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=InternationalInvestment |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2022 |title=Completion of Sale of Alcentra NY, LLC by The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation to Franklin Templeton |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20221101005892/en/Completion-of-Sale-of-Alcentra-NY-LLC-by-The-Bank-of-New-York-Mellon-Corporation-to-Franklin-Templeton |access-date=November 20, 2022 |website=Businesswire.com |language=en}} On May 31, 2023, [[Great-West Lifeco]] announced that Franklin Templeton would acquire [[Putnam Investments]] for $925 million. Putnam Investments subsidiary, [[PanAgora Asset Management]] would not be included in the acquisition.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Great-West Lifeco announces sale of Putnam Investments to Franklin Templeton |url=https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/great-west-lifeco-announces-sale-of-putnam-investments-to-franklin-templeton-854175768.html |access-date=June 8, 2023 |website=Newswire.ca |language=en}}{{Cite news |last=Masters |first=Brooke |date=May 31, 2023 |title=Franklin Templeton to buy Putnam Investments for more than $1bn |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/2fc9820c-1f3b-450c-8b1e-0f5c9b25afdb |access-date=June 8, 2023}}{{Cite web |date=May 31, 2023 |title=Great-West Lifeco announces sale of Putnam Investments to Franklin Templeton |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/great-west-lifeco-announces-sale-113500561.html |access-date=June 8, 2023 |website=Yahoo Finance |language=en-US}} The deal was completed in January 2024.{{cite web |last1=Dorbian |first1=Iris |title=Franklin Templeton scoops up Putnam Investments |url=https://www.pehub.com/franklin-templeton-scoops-up-putnam-investments/ |website=PE Hub |date=January 2, 2024}} In August 2023, [[Bloomberg News]] reported that Franklin Templeton executives in China were mandated to attend courses on [[Xi Jinping Thought]].{{Cite news |date=August 8, 2023 |title=Bankers Forced to Study Xi's Thoughts as Party Tightens Grip |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-08-08/bankers-forced-to-study-xi-s-thoughts-as-party-tightens-grip |access-date=September 18, 2023}} ==Mutual funds and ETFs== Franklin Templeton has 455 [[Open-end fund|open-ended mutual funds]] and seven [[closed-end fund]]s. Included in these are 27 state and federal tax-free income funds, an area of investment pioneered by Franklin.{{cite web |title=Mutual Funds Price and Performance {{!}} Franklin Templeton |url=https://www.franklintempleton.com/investor/investments-and-solutions/investment-options/mutual-funds/ |website=Franklintempleton.com}} Prominent funds include the Templeton Growth Fund, Inc. (opened 1954), the Mutual Shares fund (opened 1949), and the Mutual Discovery Fund (opened 1992) and the Templeton Growth (Euro) Fund. The Franklin Income Fund (FKINX) is a [[mutual fund]] in Morningstar's "conservative allocation" category and "large/value" style box. The fund was created in 1948 and has paid uninterrupted [[dividend]]s for 60 years. The Franklin Income Fund is constructed primarily of dividend-paying stocks and bonds (2%). Franklin Templeton launched its first exchange-traded funds (ETFs) in 2013. By 2021, these included 55 active, smart beta/multifactor and passively managed ETFs in the U.S, with US$9.7 billion in assets under management.{{Cite news|title=Franklin Templeton launches first ETF|url=https://www.etf.com/sections/features/20369-franklin-templeton-launches-first-etf.html|access-date=November 5, 2013|newspaper=ETF.com}}{{Cite news|title=Franklin Templeton Plans to Convert Two Mutual Funds to ETFs|url=https://www.franklintempleton.com/press-releases/2021/franklin-templeton-plans-to-convert-two-mutual-funds-to-etfs|access-date=December 14, 2021}} In 2021, Franklin Templeton launched the first "tokenised" US mutual fund as a pilot{{snd}}it uses a [[blockchain]] to process transactions and record share ownership. The technology is provided by the [[Stellar (payment network)|Stellar network]] and Blockchain Administrator, a Delaware company. The OnChain US Government Money Fund pilot started with $1.4M of seed money and investment from employees. The automated administration can trade around the clock and removes the need for brokerages, which should result in a "highly significant decrease in fees". However, the fund actually has a high level of costs because of its small size and the fact that, as a pilot, it is maintaining traditional records in parallel.{{Cite news |date=December 10, 2021 |title=Blockchain-powered breakthrough on mutual fund |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/fd57521c-a2e9-415b-9c4f-4f74b4587f9e |access-date=August 24, 2022}}{{Cite web |title=SEC filing: form N-1A |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1786958/000113743919000429/fttn1a092019.htm |access-date=August 24, 2022 |website=Sec.gov}} In February 2025, Franklin Templeton launched a spot crypto exchange-traded fund that holds a combination of roughly 80% bitcoin and 20% ether.{{cite web|url=https://www.pionline.com/exchange-traded-funds/franklin-templeton-launches-its-first-etf-multiple-cryptocurrencies/ |title=Franklin Templeton launches its first ETF with multiple cryptocurrencies| first=Palash|last=Ghosh|work=Pensions&Investments|date=February 20, 2025|access-date=July 31, 2025}} That same month Franklin applied with the SEC for a spot Solana ETF.{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/franklin-templeton-files-solana-etf-crypto-interest-expands-beyond-bitcoin-2025-02-21/ |title=Franklin Templeton files for Solana ETF as crypto interest extract: Franklin Resources, Inc. is an American multinational investment management holding company that, together with its subsidiaries, is referred to as Franklin Templeton; it is a global investment firm founded in New York City in 1947 as Franklin Distributors, Inc. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol BEN, in honor of Benjamin Franklin, for whom the company is named, and who was admired by founder Rupert Johnson Sr. The firm became the world's largest asset managers, providing services operating in 150 countries. In 1973, the company's headquarters moved from New York to San Mateo, California.
